headline: Agents Meet Your Figma Canvas
subheadline: Big moves this week: Figma's AI agents now design on canvas, Claude Code hit an insane 30+ iterations in April, and your MCP integration just got way more interesting.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma launches AI agents that design directly on the canvas
sections.description: This is the big one. Figma announced at Schema that AI agents can now work directly on the Figma canvas — designing, not just assisting. For someone building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for a white-label design system, this changes the game. It means the platform is officially moving toward agent-driven workflows, which validates exactly the direction you're heading.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Why Figma's MCP update is a bigger deal than any AI demo
sections.description: This piece digs into the March 2026 MCP release sequence and why Cursor built a new interface from scratch to work with it. It also covers the developer backlash — useful context as you bridge the design-dev gap with your own MCP work. Written just 6 days ago so it's fresh.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Claude Code April 2026 changelog: 30+ versions from Opus 4.6 to 1M context
sections.description: Claude Code has been on a tear — 30+ version iterations in March-April alone. The highlights that matter for you: Opus 4.6 with a 1M context window (imagine feeding your entire design system), NO_FLICKER rendering, and /powerup interactive tutorials for team onboarding. This directly impacts what's possible with your Claude + Figma MCP setup.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma's 2026 updates quietly redefine design-dev handoff
sections.description: Designers can now branch, commit, and merge Figma files directly to GitHub/GitLab — with version history linked to commit hashes. This is a fundamental shift in how design systems get maintained. For your white-label sport apps, this could mean tighter version control across client variants without leaving Figma.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Design systems as dynamic infrastructure, not static libraries
sections.description: The mental model is shifting: leading companies now treat design systems as data-driven infrastructure that feeds both human interfaces AND AI agents. This means your design tokens and component architecture aren't just for designers and devs anymore — they're the instruction set for AI agents that generate UI. Your MCP project is already positioned at this intersection.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Lovable 2.0 — now with Chat Mode for conversational app building
sections.description: Lovable just launched 2.0 with a Chat Mode that lets you talk through complex features before building. Given you're already vibe-coding with Lovable, this could save you serious credits by planning outside the builder first. They also launched 'Lovable Shipped' — a 6-week program with $3M in perks to go from idea to product.

sections.label: Did you know
sections.title: 47% of design systems now include comprehensive accessibility guidelines at the component level
sections.description: Up significantly from prior years. The new frontier is AI-augmented design systems that enforce accessibility automatically. If you're architecting a white-label system, baking a11y into tokens and components now means AI agents can inherit those rules by default — no manual audits per client.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If AI agents can now design on the Figma canvas, what's the designer's new leverage?
sections.description: With agents handling layout and component assembly, the premium moves to system architecture, brand judgment, and orchestrating the right constraints for AI to work within. Your design system expertise isn't being automated — it's becoming the control layer. Worth sitting with as you think about your next role: product builder who designs the rules, not the screens.
